when_to_use: cool or modal jazz where a small motif gains meaning through silence, patient modal color, and restrained horn conversation rather than chord traffic, 100-125 BPM

defaults.feel: brushed swing, floating and gently behind the beat, no hard accents

signature_moves: So What voicing on Dm7: stacked 4ths capped by a major 3rd, creating openness that invites melodic interpretation instead of defining it
modal half-step shift: D Dorian -> Eb Dorian for the bridge, making the same melodic temperament feel suddenly suspended in different light
minor stepwise cell: Dm7 -> Em7, used as a small change of floor rather than a functional progression
pianoless counterpoint: remove the chordal instrument and let two horn lines imply the mode through guide tones and independent motion
cadence_options: no functional cadence; let a modal section change meaning through motif, register, or ensemble density before shifting modes
bridge resolution by returning from the half-step-up mode to home Dorian, heard as recognition rather than dominant-tonic closure
avoid: fast ii-V-I movement; the mode is a field for listening and melodic development, not a route to navigate
comping on every beat; punctuation should respond to phrases and silence, not fill the canvas

hook_archetypes.name: three-notes-then-air
hook_archetypes.rhythm: state three notes, leave 1-2 bars of real silence, then return with one displacement or changed ending so the rest becomes part of the theme
hook_archetypes.contour: remain close to the mode's defining color, such as the Dorian natural 6th, and let one later version avoid the expected target
hook_archetypes.first_appears: Head, lead horn alone over the bass pedal before the ensemble begins interpreting it

hook_archetypes.name: line-across-still-water
hook_archetypes.rhythm: long held guide tones separated by breath, with no need to mark every barline
hook_archetypes.contour: smooth minimal movement that feels sung across the static mode rather than generated from chord changes
hook_archetypes.first_appears: Intro, above the pedal point before the full head enters

intro-pedal.note_lengths: very sparse; allow the bass pedal and brush texture to make the first statement before the lead commits
intro-pedal.contour: either absent or one bare guide-tone fragment that suggests the mode without summarizing it
intro-pedal.placement: soft and unaccented, with no strong downbeat claim

head.note_lengths: 2-3 note statements followed by 1-2 bars of rest, treating silence as the second half of every phrase
head.contour: unison or simple counterpoint between horns, calm enough that interval character remains audible
head.placement: close to the grid, with expression carried by tone and spacing rather than timing distortion

solo.note_lengths: repeat, rotate, and thin one short motif rather than running scales continuously
solo.contour: explore the mode's characteristic tones until their emotional function changes, instead of outlining nonexistent chord traffic
solo.placement: close to the grid while comping remains sparse and reactive

outro.note_lengths: return to the head motif, then increase the silence between fragments until only one suspended tone remains
outro.contour: thin toward a mute-held note whose lack of resolution feels intentional
outro.placement: relax further as the piece recedes

drum_skeleton.low_energy: continuous brush swish, barely audible feathered kick, and soft pedal hi-hat on 2 and 4 create a floor that seems to float
drum_skeleton.mid_energy: make the brush texture slightly more present and add rare soft ride observations, preserving the absence of hard accents
drum_skeleton.high_energy: increase ensemble and contrapuntal activity rather than drum force; even the fullest point remains brushed, light, and uncommanding

arrangement_defaults.layout_rules: begin with the bass pedal and brushes as an open landscape. Piano enters only with occasional quartal punctuation. Lead horn states the motif without accompaniment trying to explain it; second horn arrives later as a listener who has found a different answer. Shift the bridge mode by a half-step so the same restraint feels newly unsettled. During solos, comping should react to spaces rather than provide constant support. End by returning the motif, then allowing silence to outgrow it.

anti_boredom_rules: leave 1-2 bars of real silence after short melodic statements; the silence must remain audible even when the ensemble is present
keep harmony modal and static within a section; development must come from motif, counterpoint, register, timbre, and the sanctioned mode shift
piano comping, when present, must answer or frame a phrase rather than occupy every beat
the three-note hook must return with rhythmic displacement, a changed final note, altered speaker, or different amount of silence
drums never harden into an accented backbeat; energy must be created by attention and interaction rather than impact

bass_behavior.role: modal pedal and sparse melodic anchor
bass_behavior.rhythmic_relationship: sits slightly behind the brushed pulse and avoids functional walking pressure
bass_behavior.density: sparse pedal in the head, selectively more active in solos
bass_behavior.articulation: warm upright sustain with ample decay

groove_intent.feel: floating brushed modal swing with no hard backbeat
groove_intent.snare: continuous brush texture rather than discrete backbeats
groove_intent.hihat: soft foot close on beats 2 and 4
groove_intent.ensemble_relationship: space and horn counterpoint create energy while rhythm section stays restrained

distinguishing_traits: static Dorian canvas instead of functional harmony
medium-tempo brushed ensemble with optional pianoless counterpoint
